title: Linear-time sorts
description:
Sort without comparing elements:

```cpp
struct Score { std::string name; int points; };     // points from 0 to 100

std::vector<Score> rankScores(const std::vector<Score>& scores);   // highest points first; equal points keep input order
void radixSort(std::vector<std::uint32_t>& a);                     // LSD, base 256, four passes
void radixSortSigned(std::vector<std::int32_t>& a);                // negatives too
void sortCodes(std::vector<std::string>& codes);                   // all the same length; LSD by character
```

- `rankScores` is a **stable counting sort** with prefix sums (lesson 3.05), in descending order of points. Points outside 0 to 100 throw `std::invalid_argument`.
- `radixSort`: four stable counting-sort passes over the bytes, lowest byte first, with one buffer.
- `radixSortSigned`: flip the sign bit (`x ^ 0x80000000` on the unsigned bit pattern) so that negative numbers sort first, radix sort, and flip it back.
- `sortCodes`: strings of equal length (throw `std::invalid_argument` otherwise), one stable pass per position from the last, 256 buckets (use `unsigned char`).
- No `std::sort` or `std::stable_sort`.
hints: For descending order with counting sort, map each score to a bucket number `100 - points`, so bucket 0 holds the 100s; then the usual ascending counting sort over buckets gives descending points.
Flipping the top bit maps the signed range in order onto the unsigned range: `INT_MIN` becomes 0, `-1` becomes `0x7FFFFFFF`, `0` becomes `0x80000000`.
rules: Sort by counting, not by comparing.

rules.message: Sort by counting, not by comparing.
